when: no session: auto-CRUD (which adds `docs` and, for an owner-scoped read or a stale credential, a `hint`) and most built-in routes. A flow's `auth: required` gate answers `{"error":"Unauthorized"}`, so branch on the status, not the text

a cookie-session write without a valid X-CSRF-Token header or _csrf field, on auto-CRUD and flow routes. Other built-in routes spell it `invalid CSRF token`, `invalid csrf token` or `invalid csrf`, and a JSON sign-in or sign-up answers `missing or expired CSRF token: ...`, so test `error` for csrf without regard to case, then fetch a fresh token (GET /api/_csrf) and retry

body.message: no API route matches this path, or the app's access rules do not let you use it

when: no route, or a table the caller may not read (the two answers are identical, so a hidden table's existence does not leak; the message names both causes). The side routes answer the same: /api/_transaction and /api/_query for an unknown table, and record locks, share/permissions/revoke and revert for a table the caller may not read

body.message: the app's access rules do not let you create rows in services (its `write` rule under access: in app.yaml)

when: a create, update or delete the access rules refuse on a table the caller may read (GET already shows it exists); a tenant-less caller on a tenant-keyed table also gets a `hint`

body.message: Record was modified by another user

when: optimistic concurrency mismatch: the row's updated_at is no longer the `_expected_updated_at` a PATCH or /api/_transaction update sent; re-read the row and retry (api({at:'concurrency'}))

a refused value; `error` is the sentence, there is no `validation failed` code and no per-field map. A create that omits a required column (NOT NULL without a default) answers `<column> is required`, a validators.yaml rule its own `error:` text (`Validation failed: <rule>` when it has none) and an aborting before-hook its message

body.error: record is locked by another user

when: a record lock held by another user (api({at:'locks'})); the status is 409, not 423

a rate limit refused the request: a flow's `rate_limit` (this body, naming its window), the app-wide per-user/IP limiter, the ingest limit. Branch on the status, not the text, and wait for the Retry-After header when the answer has one

a write needed more space than the app's storage limit allows (see api({at:'recovery'}) storage_limit); reads and deletes still work. The check before a create answers only `error` and `detail`; branch on the status and `error`

an upload would take the app owner's account past its media storage allowance on the hosted platform (see api({at:'uploads'}) storage_allowance); nothing is stored, and files already stored keep serving and can be deleted. Same status and `error` as the database limit: `code` tells them apart

body.error: request body too large: the limit is 1.0 MB (1048576 bytes)

when: a request body over its cap: a flow's JSON body or `parse: body` step (1 MiB), or any flow or auto-CRUD body over the app's MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES (default 10 MiB). Nothing runs
flow registered but produced no respond step, or a step failed (then also message, failed_step, failed_type and reason; see api({at:'flows'}) step_failures)

a respond step referenced a value no step produced; `unresolved_refs` lists them as `<step id>.<output>`. A body that is one whole `${{ ref }}` answers `unresolved_key: "<step id>.<output>"` instead of the list. A development instance adds `available_keys`
a built-in JSON route failed on the server (see server_errors); text routes answer `list failed (request id: 3f9c2a1b7d4e5f60)`
